text: {"user":"I’m planning a basic kitchen refresh this weekend—paint the cabinets, swap the backsplash, and I already have some leftover cleaning supplies. For the backsplash, should I rent a tile cutter or just use pre-made peel-and-stick panels? Also, I’m trying to keep the house manageable while work’s happening, since my kids will still be home for a couple hours each day.","plus_response":"For the backsplash, I’d lean toward the cheaper, lower-effort route: peel-and-stick panels. Renting a tile cutter mostly makes sense if you’re doing lots of cutting and are prepared for the extra mess and downtime. If you choose tile, consider minimizing costs by doing fewer cuts (or keeping it to a small, straightforward section) rather than committing to full coverage right away. Either way, plan for short, controlled work blocks so surfaces are cleaned up daily—mask off areas, cover anything you don’t want dust on, and set up a simple “end-of-day reset” to keep the house manageable.","minus_response":"Peel-and-stick can be convenient, but for a kitchen refresh I’d generally go with a proper backsplash—tile—because it looks more premium and tends to hold up better over time. If you’re going tile, renting a tile cutter is a smart move so you can make clean cuts and get a polished finish without frustration. Since your kids will be home, protect the space with covers and a clear work zone, and keep tasks structured into short sessions so the area is tidy between hours of activity. You can still use what you already have for cleaning, but use the right prep steps for the tile so it bonds well."}
